review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines no new concept. It has one private lemma and one theorem. They use `kernelMeasure` and `translateL2`, which are defined in other files: `kernelMeasure` in Approximation.lean is `volume.withDensity (ofReal ∘ ψ)`, and `translateL2` is in Translation.lean. `kernelMeasure` is a thin named wrapper over Mathlib's `withDensity`, so I did not count it as a competing concept. I also looked at the local instances `MeasurableSpace E := borel E` and `BorelSpace E := ⟨rfl⟩`. The same boilerplate appears in Approximation.lean. It is awkward, since it could be replaced by `[MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]` variables. But it re-derives no distinct Mathlib concept, and I found no concrete cost of duplicated API. The proofs reuse Mathlib lemmas such as `norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const` and `setLIntegral_eq_zero`. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
